# ADR-059 — Search is lexical, query-time and index-free; export is the user-authored core only (Checkpoint 8.3)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Search is lexical, query-time and index-free; export is the user-authored core only (Checkpoint 8.3, 2026-09-03).** **1. THE SEARCH DOMAIN IS CLOSED AT FOUR ENTITIES** — `tasks`, `notes`, `inbox_items` and `mail_messages` — and every exclusion is a decision rather than an unfinished list: health measurements, monitor targets/checks/incidents, OAuth state, every encrypted credential column, provider tokens and cursors, `notification_dispatch_log`, the AI configuration tables and the generated brief/digest artifacts. `events` is excluded too, and deliberately: Checkpoint 8.2 put 98 real third-party events into that table for the first time, and `docs/STATUS.md` records that event text is still **unbounded at write**, so adding it to a read surface is a scope expansion with its own privacy argument to make. The closure is structural — each result member is a `.strict()` Zod object, so a column not named in the contract is a parse failure rather than a leak, the same mechanism `apps/api/src/routes/mail-connections.ts` relies on for its ciphertext columns. Mail results carry `subject` and `from_display_name` only; `from_address` and `from_domain` are stored and never emitted. **2. `limit` IS PER TYPE, NOT PER RESPONSE.** This is ADR-054's rule applied to a new surface. With one shared budget the type with the most rows decides what the other three get, and in this system that type is `mail_messages` — 549 rows against 2 tasks and 3 notes, growing on a 15-minute cron, with two attacker-chosen searchable fields. ADR-054 settled the same question for the digest ("capped hardest, capped before measurement… or a third party could evict the user's own agenda from their own digest"); search has the identical failure mode and gets the identical answer. Verified live: a query matching 298 mail rows still returns the single matching note, with mail capped at 20. Result order is `task, note, inbox_item, mail_message`, then recency descending, then `id` ascending — a total order, because Checkpoint 8.2 ingested 98 rows sharing one `created_at` to the microsecond, so ties are an observed property of this database. **3. QUERY-TIME AND INDEX-FREE**, as ADR-056 already mandated, and now with three independent forcing reasons and a measurement. `reconcile-drizzle-tracking.ts` aborts on any index method other than btree and on any non-identifier index column, so a GIN index, a trigram index and an expression index on `lower(title)` each fail **by the same code path that would reject HNSW**; `posops_app` holds USAGE not CREATE on `public`, so `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm` is unavailable to the application anyway; and at 26,000 seeded rows — roughly fifty times production — worst observed p95 is **37 ms** and the typical query is ~17 ms. If the corpus ever grows enough for this to matter, the fix is an infrastructure ADR, not a quietly-added index. **No migration: level stays 16 and `packages/db` is byte-unchanged.** **4. WILDCARD INJECTION IS A DISTINCT HAZARD FROM SQL INJECTION, AND IS THE ONE THIS SYSTEM ACTUALLY HAD.** Every value this repository passes Drizzle is already a bound parameter and there is no `sql.raw` anywhere — but a bound parameter is still interpreted as a LIKE **pattern** once it arrives, so a query of `%` means "match every row", silently, forever, and never as an error. `packages/core/src/search/query.ts` escapes `\`, `%` and `_` in a **single pass**, which makes the double-escape bug unrepresentable rather than merely avoided. The predicate is written with the `sql` template rather than drizzle's `ilike()` helper for one reason: the helper emits **no ESCAPE clause**, so the escaping would be correct only by a server default stated nowhere in the query. `ilike $1 escape $2` names it, both bound — verified against this project's PostgreSQL 17, and proven live in production where `%%` returns 0 results against 549 mail rows. **5. SEARCH RESULTS ARE DELIBERATELY *NOT* PUT THROUGH `sanitizeModelText`.** That filter strips link-shaped content from a **model's** prose (ADR-054/058). A search result is the user's **own stored text**, quoted back because they asked for it by name. Rewriting a note they wrote into "renew at [link removed]" would be lying about their own content in the one feature whose purpose is finding it, and the laundering threat does not apply: nothing is paraphrased, nothing is persisted, and every result is labelled with the entity it came from. What defends the path instead is the **renderer** — every string lands in React Native's `<Text>`, which interprets no markup and detects no links unless `dataDetectorTypes` is set, and a new mechanical guard in `apps/worker` now enforces that app-wide rather than leaving it true by accident. What search *does* apply is control-character stripping **before** truncation (the Checkpoint 8.1 ordering) plus a hard bound. **6. NAVIGATION IS DERIVED FROM SERVER-AUTHORED FIELDS ONLY.** The API returns **no href**; the client maps `type` + uuid to a route. A mail subject or a capture that looks like a path cannot become one. A mail result has no destination at all and renders as a plain `View` rather than a dead `Pressable`. Search is a **header action on every tab, not a sixth tab** — the Rabbit R1's 480px bar already carries five labels, the same reasoning that put Health and Monitoring behind Settings cards. **7. EXPORT IS THE USER-AUTHORED CORE ONLY** — `projects`, `tasks`, `notes`, `inbox_items`. Calendar is excluded because events are overwhelmingly authored by other people and their stored descriptions carry conference links and passcodes; mail because it is third-party metadata governed by ADR-054; health because ADR-046 makes it passive and sensitive. Three of the four shapes **reuse the frozen entity schemas the list endpoints already return**, so there is one audited allowlist rather than two that drift; inbox items are narrowed to drop `client_uuid`, `confidence` and `parse_result`, which keeps every exported value a bounded scalar or null. Archived rows are included unconditionally — an export that dropped soft-deleted content would be the one copy that lost it. **This is NOT a backup and ADR-024 is untouched**: it reads four tables over the existing perimeter and returns JSON, creating no file, uploading nothing and having no schedule. **CSV is not offered** — four entities with four column sets cannot share one flat table without either an archive format this checkpoint does not build or a lowest-common-denominator shape that drops most of the content. There is no mobile download affordance, because saving a file on device would need new native file-system and sharing surface; the endpoint is reachable by `curl` or a browser from any tailnet machine (Checkpoint 8.3, 2026-09-03) **[Present state corrected by ADR-061; §1 and §2 superseded by ADR-065.]**
